title: USB Hotplug Capture Framework - Full Specification
description:
## Summary

A Kubernetes-native framework that automatically schedules capture workloads when USB devices are plugged into cluster nodes and tears them down on unplug. The framework uses Node Feature Discovery (NFD) to detect USB devices, applies node labels, and lets DaemonSet nodeSelectors handle scheduling. Two initial workloads: an optical disc ripper and a document scanner.

## Architecture

**Core pattern:** USB hotplug -> NFD node label -> DaemonSet scheduling -> capture -> NFS write -> notification

**Cluster environment:** Talos Linux, ArgoCD GitOps, Cilium CNI (default-deny), 1Password Connect + External Secrets Operator, Prometheus + Grafana monitoring. Storage target is a Synology NAS via NFS.

**Detection chain:**
1. NFD DaemonSet scans for USB devices, applies custom labels based on vendor/product ID
2. Smarter Device Manager exposes /dev/sr0, /dev/sg0, USB bus devices as allocatable Kubernetes resources
3. DaemonSets with nodeSelectors on NFD labels schedule pods when devices appear, remove them when devices disappear

**Shared infrastructure:**
- NFS PersistentVolume/PersistentVolumeClaim for Synology /volume1/incoming
- Cilium network policies restricting capture pod egress to NFS, notification relay, metadata APIs (OMDb, MusicBrainz), and DNS only
- Notification relay service (webhook fan-out to Discord, Pushover, NATS in Phase 2)
- Secrets via 1Password/ESO (MakeMKV license, OMDb API key, webhook tokens)

## Workload 1: Optical Disc Ripper

**Container image:** Community `automaticrippingmachine/automatic-ripping-machine` (confirmed arm64 multi-arch support)

**Hardware:** Pioneer BDR-XS07UHD (USB 3.0, bus-powered, LibreDrive compatible for UHD Blu-ray)

**Behavior:**
- ARM (Automatic Ripping Machine) handles disc detection, type ID, ripping orchestration, metadata lookup
- MakeMKV for video disc decryption/extraction (LibreDrive mode for UHD)
- abcde for audio CD ripping to FLAC
- dd/mkisofs for data disc ISO creation
- No transcoding at capture (HANDBRAKE_PRESET: disabled) -- raw MKV output
- Auto-ejects disc on completion, polls for next insertion
- Post-rip hook POSTs notification event to relay service

**Disc type routing:**
- UHD Blu-ray / Blu-ray / DVD -> MKV in /incoming/video/{Title} ({Year})/
- Audio CD -> FLAC in /incoming/audio/{Artist} - {Album}/
- Data disc -> ISO in /incoming/data/{label}_{date}.iso

**Resource profile (Raspberry Pi 4):**
- CPU: ~40-60% of one core during rip (I/O bound, not compute bound)
- Memory: ~600-800 MB total (MakeMKV + ARM web UI + framework overhead)
- Minimum 4 GB Pi 4; 8 GB comfortable
- arm64 confirmed viable: MakeMKV ships native arm64 binaries, ARM Docker image publishes linux/arm64

## Workload 2: Document Scanner

**Container image:** Custom-built (Ubuntu 24.04 + SANE + epsonscan2 + Python session manager + Flask web UI)

**Hardware:** Epson DS-1630 (USB 3.0, flatbed + 50-sheet ADF, duplex via ADF, 600 DPI optical)

**Scan parameters (always maximum fidelity):**
- 600 DPI, 24-bit color, TIFF (uncompressed or LZW)
- Duplex enabled by default for ADF
- No blank page skipping at capture (downstream concern)

**Two scanning modes:**
- ADF mode: Load stack, all pages scanned sequentially, session closes when feeder empties
- Flatbed mode: One page at a time, consecutive scans grouped by 90-second idle timeout, "new document" button in web UI forces session boundary

**Session lifecycle:** Pages accumulate -> session closes (ADF empty / idle timeout / manual close) -> manifest.json written -> notification POST -> ready for next session

**Web UI:** Status page, manual scan trigger, new document / close session buttons, duplex toggle, session review with thumbnails, idle timeout config

**Resource profile (Raspberry Pi 4):**
- CPU: <20% of one core (I/O bound -- USB transfer + NFS write)
- Memory: ~300-500 MB total (SANE + one TIFF page buffer + Python + Flask)
- 2 GB Pi 4 is tight but possible; 4 GB comfortable
- arm64 fully supported (epsonscan2, SANE, Python/Flask all in Ubuntu arm64 repos)

## Notification System

**Event schema (v1.0):** JSON with schema_version, source, event_type, timestamp, output_path, media_type, metadata, node_name

**Phase 1 transport:** Webhook POST to cluster-internal notification relay, fan-out to configured destinations

**Phase 2 transport:** NATS subject for OpenClaw agent integration

**Failure handling:** Exponential backoff retry (3 attempts: 5s/30s/120s), dead-letter to /incoming/notifications/dead-letter/ on final failure, periodic dead-letter replay

## NAS Directory Structure

/volume1/incoming/
- video/{Title} ({Year})/*.mkv + metadata.json
- audio/{Artist} - {Album}/*.flac + metadata.json
- data/{label}_{date}.iso
- scans/sessions/{timestamp}_{session-id}/*.tiff + manifest.json
- scans/documents/ (downstream classification output)
- scans/books/ (downstream book reconstruction output)
- notifications/ (dead-letter audit log)

## What This Delivers (Phase 1)

- Fully automated disc ripping: plug in drive, insert disc, walk away, get organized MKV/FLAC/ISO on NAS
- Fully automated document scanning: plug in scanner, load ADF or use flatbed, get organized TIFFs on NAS
- Ephemeral workloads: zero resource consumption when devices are unplugged
- GitOps-managed: all manifests in repo, deployed via ArgoCD
- Monitoring: Prometheus metrics (rip duration, disc type counts, scan sessions, pages/session, notification success/failure) + Grafana dashboard
- Secure: Cilium default-deny egress, secrets from 1Password, no plaintext credentials

## What This Does NOT Deliver

- No transcoding or compression at capture time (downstream concern)
- No document classification, OCR, or text extraction (Phase 2, requires Mac Studio M5 for local LLM inference)
- No book reconstruction or EPUB generation (Phase 2)
- No reMarkable delivery integration (Phase 2)
- No NATS-based event transport (Phase 2, webhook relay only in Phase 1)
- No OpenClaw agent integration (Phase 2)
- No local embedding/search index for scanned documents (Phase 2)
- No physical "scan" button or GPIO/NFC document boundary button (Phase 3)
- No multi-scanner support (Phase 3)
- No barcode/QR code detection (Phase 3)
- Scanner does NOT do blank page detection/removal -- that is a downstream classification concern
- Scanner does NOT classify or split multi-document ADF sessions -- downstream LLM pipeline handles this

## Open Questions

- NFD scan interval: default (~60s) vs aggressive (~15s) -- start with default, tune later
- Scanner hardware button support via SANE button API -- needs testing on actual hardware
- Smarter Device Manager vs custom device plugin -- evaluate during implementation
- Flatbed idle timeout (90s proposed) -- configurable via web UI, tune with real usage
- Phase 1 notification transport: simple webhook relay (decided) vs NATS from the start
close_reason: Phase 1 implementation complete. All 23 child beads closed, 205 tests passing.

title: umbrella: hardware-attached pods receive host udev events
description: Today the optical-ripper and document-scanner containers run their own udev daemons but receive zero host kernel uevents because (a) PSS=restricted on the recognizer ns blocks privileged: true, (b) no hostPath mount of /run/udev so the in-container udev cannot subscribe to the host udev daemon's socket, (c) smarter-device-manager only exposes /dev entries, never forwards uevents. Net effect: ARM sees the drive at startup but never sees disc insert/eject; scanner pod (when enabled) sees the USB device but no page-ready or attach events. Closing this requires four pieces: a namespace-architecture decision, chart wiring for both hardware pods, a notification-event schema bump, and an end-to-end SLO benchmark.
acceptance_criteria: Inserting a disc on johnny's drive results in a disc-detected notification event arriving at the relay within 5 seconds for CD/DVD media. Same kind of liveness for scanner page-ready events.

title: end-to-end flatbed scanner acceptance test (document-scanner)
description:
The chart's documentScanner DaemonSet has never been enabled or tested in-cluster. With opticalRipper proven (NFD + smarter-device-manager are in place), the prereqs are satisfied for documentScanner too.

What needs to happen:

1. Physical setup
   - Plug the Epson DS-1630 (or other supported scanner) into a USB port on a target node. Optical-ripper's pattern uses johnny; flatbed may use the same node or a different one.
   - Confirm the NFD rule (gitops configmap-nfd-worker-recognizer.yaml) labels that node with recognizer.io/device-scanner=<model>. If no such NFD rule exists yet for the scanner, file a gitops bead like the optical-drive one (gitops-evm1 pattern).

2. Chart wiring
   - documentScanner.enabled=true in the cluster's HelmRelease.
   - Set documentScanner.nodeSelector to the NFD-emitted label key/value.
   - Verify smarter-devices/bus-usb=1 resource request lands and the pod schedules on the labeled node.

3. End-to-end test
   - Trigger a scan via whatever interface the document-scanner image exposes (HTTP endpoint? cron-driven? button-press?). Look at images/document-scanner/ source for the trigger mechanism.
   - Verify the scan writes a file to the chart's data PVC.
   - Verify a notification event fires through the notification-relay (event_type likely document-scan-complete or similar; check notification-event v1.x schema for the source/event_type enum).
   - Verify the file becomes deliverable to glovebox (does the delivery flow even fit single-file scans, or is this a different transport?).

4. Open question: does glovebox have a media_type for scanned documents (image/pdf or doc/scan or similar)? If not, file a follow-up to extend its mediaAllowList (cf. the glovebox-4enb pattern).

Scope explicitly excludes: enabling the chart-default node-feature-rule for additional scanner models; multi-scanner sharing; OCR. Get one scanner + one node + one successful scan + delivery on the wire first.
acceptance_criteria: documentScanner pod schedules on the scanner-labeled node, picks up USB passthrough, performs a scan (driven however the image's entrypoint expects), writes a file to the PVC, emits a recognizer notification event, and the file lands in glovebox via the archive-delivery path or whatever the design says.

title: archive-importer: Meta/Facebook export support
description:
Add a second Provider beside GoogleTakeoutProvider that recognizes Meta/Facebook data exports (JSON variant). Detection: presence of personal_information/profile_information/profile_information.json with a profile_v2 (or profile_information_v2) key. Sample on disk: /mnt/c/Users/steve/Downloads/facebook-stevenwagner5895834-2026-04-12-WkObY8Ht.zip (332MB, 801 files, 349 JSON + media). First cut: depth-1 matchers for the 8 top-level dirs (ads_information, apps_and_websites_off_of_facebook, connections, logged_information, personal_information, preferences, security_and_login_information, your_facebook_activity). Depth-2 expansion (per-sub-dir matchers like your_facebook_activity/posts vs /messages) is a follow-up if glovebox or downstream wants finer routing.

Refactor work needed in main.go to make it multi-provider: today provider is hardcoded to GoogleTakeoutProvider, unrecognized media_type is hardcoded archive/google-takeout/unrecognized-subtree, complete-event media_type is hardcoded archive/google-takeout, and unrecognized path is prefixed with literal Takeout/. All four spots need to be provider-aware.

Instagram exports are out of scope for this bead -- file a follow-up if user has one.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-provider dispatch in main.go; MetaProvider returns true for the Facebook sample; all 8 top-level dirs match without unrecognized; local end-to-end runZipImport produces a manifest with 8 recognized subtrees, 0 unrecognized; tests pass; go vet clean.
close_reason: Implemented: MetaProvider with profile_v2/profile_information_v2 detection + 8 depth-1 matchers; multi-provider dispatch in main.go. End-to-end test on a real 332MB Facebook export: 8/8 recognized, 0 unrecognized, 9 events. Tests pass, go vet clean.

title: Chart: persist MakeMKV settings.conf via init container
description: MakeMKV key is in Vault but the optical-ripper pod uses an emptyDir for /home/arm, so the manually-injected /home/arm/.MakeMKV/settings.conf is wiped on every pod restart. Add an init container that reads the key from an env var (sourced from a Vault-backed Secret via ESO) and writes settings.conf into the home volume before the main container starts. RED: rip fails with 'version too old' after pod restart. GREEN: rip works on every pod restart without manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Pod restart preserves working MakeMKV key without operator action; rip-test on a known disc succeeds end-to-end yielding actual files.

title: Chart: silence PSS warnings on archive-importer container
description: Every archive-importer Job pod emits 4 PodSecurity baseline warnings: allowPrivilegeEscalation, capabilities.drop=ALL, runAsNonRoot, seccompProfile. PSS is enforced at 'restricted:latest' on the recognizer ns. Currently they're warnings (admission allows the pod) but they're noisy and would block enforcement bumps. Pod already has runAsUser/runAsGroup/fsGroup=1000 from earlier fixes; just need the container-level securityContext block.
acceptance_criteria: Pod admission succeeds with no PSS warnings; runs as uid 1000, capabilities ALL dropped, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, seccompProfile RuntimeDefault.

title: Recognizer HTTP-push client for glovebox archive-delivery endpoint
description:
## Why this issue exists

Companion to glovebox-lfov (now resolved: spec 13 + endpoint shipped). Glovebox handoff doc lives in their repo at docs/handoffs/recognizer-archive-delivery.md and supersedes any client-side guesses we made earlier.

## What the client needs to do

For each subtree in archive-layout-manifest.v1.json's subtrees_recognized list:

- Build per-subtree Upload-Metadata (base64-encoded values):
  - archive_id: <hash-prefix>-<filename>-<subtree-key> (idempotency key)
  - archive_filename: original archive name
  - media_type: archive/mbox (raw mbox), archive/google-takeout-subtree (tar of a Takeout subdir), archive/generic-tarball (Meta or other unknown-tar)
  - matcher_id: free-form correlation id, "google-takeout/mail", "meta-facebook/ads-information", etc.
  - provider: "recognizer" (the spec calls it our source-id; glovebox source-id "recognizer-smoke-test" to start)
  - sha256: lowercase hex of body bytes
  - size_bytes: decimal int, must equal Upload-Length exactly
  - subtree_relative_path: only for archive/google-takeout-subtree
- For raw-file deliveries: use existing manifest.Source.SHA256 + size_bytes (mbox case; subtree IS the whole archive)
- For directory subtree deliveries: stream tar.gz into a temp file, capturing sha256 + size in the same pass
- Talk tus.io v1.0.0 over http://glovebox.glovebox.svc.cluster.local:9091:
  - POST /v1/archives with Upload-Length + Upload-Metadata, capture Location
  - PATCH Location in 16-64 MiB chunks until Upload-Length reached
  - On 303 from POST: idempotent replay, skip
  - On 5xx / 429: retry with Retry-After
  - HEAD on resume to discover server's current Upload-Offset
- On success: write Delivery record into manifest.Deliveries (new optional field)
- On non-retryable 4xx: record failure into Delivery with FailureReason, emit delivery-failed event

## Chart changes

- ExternalSecret targeting Vault path secret/glovebox/ingest-tokens/<source-id> → K8s Secret recognizer-glovebox-ingest-token
- CronJob env: GLOVEBOX_INGEST_URL, GLOVEBOX_INGEST_TOKEN (from Secret), GLOVEBOX_INGEST_SOURCE_ID
- New Values keys: gloveboxIngest.enabled, gloveboxIngest.url, gloveboxIngest.sourceID, gloveboxIngest.token.vaultPath

## Operator step needed

kubectl label ns recognizer name=openclaw-recognizer
(without this, glovebox's NetworkPolicy drops every packet at L4)

## Notes / what changed since the bead was first filed

- Wire is tus.io v1.0.0 not custom multipart (huge win: resumable, well-specified)
- Glovebox computes sha256 during PATCH and verifies at finalize; we must compute it client-side too so the metadata matches
- No "completion ping" -- glovebox-c9zt watches archives/ and picks up new dirs automatically (spec 9 mbox-importer)
- Glovebox allow-listed 4 media_types; Meta exports go in as archive/generic-tarball (matcher_id carries the Meta-specific tag)
- Reserved metadata keys delivered_by/delivered_at are written server-side; do NOT set them client-side
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] HTTP client implementation under images/archive-importer/internal/delivery/
- [ ] Streams directory subtrees as tar, streams raw-file subtrees as-is
- [ ] Bearer-token auth from env, retries 5xx/429, surfaces 4xx body in errors
- [ ] Idempotent across job re-runs (consults manifest before re-delivering)
- [ ] Manifest gains a "deliveries" section with per-subtree receipts
- [ ] Notification events emitted for delivery-complete and delivery-failed
- [ ] Chart wires the env vars and ExternalSecret; glovebox-p1zx tells us the Vault path
- [ ] End-to-end: 12GB mbox delivered without 413; all 4 in-cluster Takeout zips' subtrees delivered
close_reason: Shipped in v0.4.0. internal/delivery/ implements tus.io v1.0.0 client + tar/raw streamer + Orchestrator that maps recognizer media_types to glovebox's 4-value allow-list. Chart wiring (ExternalSecret + CronJob env + Values toggle) gated behind archiveImporter.gloveboxIngest.enabled=false default. 16 unit tests green. End-to-end smoke depends on operator labeling the recognizer namespace name=openclaw-recognizer and seeding Vault path secret/glovebox/ingest-tokens/recognizer-smoke-test.

title: Archive Importer for Google Takeout (spec 03 V1)
description:
Implement the archive importer pattern from spec 01 for Google Takeout, per spec 03 (about to land).

Scope (option B from brainstorm):
- New container image and binary 'archive-importer' (Go)
- Container unpacker (zip; tar.gz and 7z later)
- Google Takeout provider detector + ~15 subtree matchers
- Notification event schema bump to v1.1
- New archive-layout-manifest.v1 schema
- Chart workload (suspended CronJob template + ConfigMap + ServiceAccount)
- CI job (build:archive-importer via kaniko)
- Consumer-facing output format documentation in spec 03

Deferred:
- Meta export recognizer (follow-up spec 04)
- Inbox watcher (V2)
- tar.gz / 7z unpackers (V1 is zip-only per usual Takeout shipping format)

Spec: docs/specs/03-archive-importer-google-takeout.md

title: Recognizer: GitLab CI + Helm chart + gitops deployment
description: Get recognizer building cleanly on gitlab.orac.local (images and a Helm chart), and deploy it to the orac cluster via the sibling gitops repo. Replaces the existing GitHub Actions CI and the raw Kustomize manifests under manifests/. See docs/specs/02-recognizer-gitlab-deploy.md for the design.
notes: Phase F MR opened: steve/gitops!4 (https://gitlab.orac.local/steve/gitops/-/merge_requests/4). Wires recognizer into the apps tier via Flux, pinned to chart 0.1.1. notification-relay enabled; doc-scanner + optical-ripper disabled in HelmRelease values pending NFD + smarter-device-manager (umbrella: gitops-jakd, individual: gitops-touw + gitops-evm1). v0.1.0 (storage backend selector) and v0.1.1 (chart docs) both published to registry.orac.local. archiver MRs !1, !2, !3 all merged. Phase G (cluster verify + acceptance test from user's optical-ripper scenario) blocks on gitops MR merging AND the two infra installs landing.

comments.author: Steven Wagner

title: Write spec: 01-archive-importer-pattern
description: Establish the archive-importer pattern spec in archiver, and the docs/specs/ directory convention. Cross-cutting architecture: extends archiver's physical-media capture pattern to digital archives (Google Takeout, WhatsApp export, Slack export, etc.). Taxonomy of layers (container unpacker -> layout recognizer -> format handler -> destination). Extends notification-event.v1 schema to v1.1 with archive/* media types. Documents how glovebox (and other destinations like Immich) consume these events. No recognizer code in V1 -- schema and architectural doc only. The Google Takeout outer recognizer and Mail subrecognizer are V2. Output: docs/specs/01-archive-importer-pattern.md
close_reason: Spec written and committed (c483034). User approved for implementation.

title: ArgoCD Application manifest
description:
Create the ArgoCD Application resource that deploys the entire capture namespace from this repo.

## Deliverables
- manifests/argocd/application.yaml

## TDD approach
- Validate manifest with kubeconform (with ArgoCD CRD schemas)
- Write test that validates Application source points to this repo and targets the capture namespace

## Exit criteria
- ArgoCD Application targets the capture namespace
- Source references this Git repo (URL parameterized)
- Path covers all manifests (manifests/ directory or Kustomize root)
- Sync policy: automated with self-heal and prune enabled

title: Scanner Dockerfile and DaemonSet manifest
description:
Package the document scanner session manager as a container and create its Kubernetes DaemonSet, Service, and ConfigMap manifests.

## Deliverables
- images/document-scanner/Dockerfile
- manifests/document-scanner/daemonset.yaml
- manifests/document-scanner/service.yaml
- manifests/document-scanner/configmap.yaml (session manager config: idle timeout, relay URL, scan params)

## TDD approach
- Validate Kubernetes manifests with kubeconform
- Test Dockerfile builds successfully
- Write test that validates DaemonSet structure matches scanner requirements

## Exit criteria
- Dockerfile installs SANE, epsonscan2, and the session manager binary/app
- Multi-stage build to minimize image size (build stage + runtime stage)
- nodeSelector matches NFD label: openclaw.io/device-scanner: epson-ds-1630
- Resource limits request smarter-devices/bus-usb: 1
- Volume mounts: NFS PVC at /out, scanner config ConfigMap at /etc/scanner
- Labels include app.kubernetes.io/part-of: capture-framework
- Service exposes web UI port 8080
- ConfigMap includes configurable idle timeout, relay URL, scan resolution, color mode
- kubeconform passes on all manifests
notes:
Go binary via multi-stage Dockerfile. Much smaller final image than Python+SANE.
Cross-bead consistency test: validate that nodeSelector label (openclaw.io/device-scanner) matches NFD rule label, and resource limits (smarter-devices/bus-usb) match SDM config device names.

title: Scanner web UI
description:
Implement the lightweight web UI for scanner status monitoring and manual controls.

## Deliverables
- images/document-scanner/scanner-session-manager/web/ (Go HTTP handlers or templates)
- tests/scanner/test_web.py (or test_web_test.go)

## TDD approach
- Red: test GET /status returns scanner state JSON (idle/scanning/session-open, page count, recent sessions)
- Red: test POST /scan triggers a flatbed scan
- Red: test POST /session/close force-closes current session
- Red: test POST /session/new-document closes current session and opens new one
- Green: implement HTTP handlers

## Exit criteria
- GET /status returns JSON: scanner connection status, current session state, page count, recent sessions list
- GET / serves an HTML status page (server-rendered, no JS framework needed)
- POST /scan triggers a flatbed scan
- POST /session/close force-closes current session
- POST /session/new-document boundary: close current + open new
- POST /settings allows idle timeout adjustment
- GET /healthz returns 200 (liveness probe)
- All endpoints tested via HTTP test client
- pytest/go test passes
notes: Language: Go. Use net/http/httptest for endpoint tests.

title: Scanner notification dispatch
description:
Implement notification dispatch when a scan session closes: construct a notification event from session data and POST to the relay.

## Deliverables
- images/document-scanner/scanner-session-manager/notify.py (or notify.go)
- tests/scanner/test_notify.py (or test_notify_test.go)

## TDD approach
- Red: test that closing a session produces a valid notification event matching notification-event.v1 schema
- Red: test POST to relay endpoint with correct payload
- Green: implement notification construction and HTTP POST

## Exit criteria
- Constructs valid notification-event.v1 JSON from session data
- source: "document-scanner", event_type: "scan-session-complete"
- media_type: "scan/adf-session" or "scan/flatbed-session" based on input method
- metadata includes page_count, session_id, source_device
- POSTs to configurable relay URL (default: http://notification-relay.capture.svc.cluster.local:8080/event)
- Logs success/failure (relay handles its own retry; scanner just fires and logs)
- pytest/go test passes

title: Scanner manifest.json generation
description:
Implement manifest.json generation when a scan session closes. The manifest must validate against scan-session-manifest.v1 schema.

## Deliverables
- images/document-scanner/scanner-session-manager/manifest.py (or manifest.go)
- tests/scanner/test_manifest.py (or test_manifest_test.go)

## TDD approach
- Red: write test that closes a session with known pages and expects a valid manifest.json
- Red: validate generated manifest against scan-session-manifest.v1.schema.json
- Green: implement manifest generation from session state

## Exit criteria
- Generated manifest validates against scan-session-manifest.v1.schema.json
- All required fields populated: session_id, timestamps, source_device, input_method, duplex, resolution, color_mode, page_count, pages array, output_path
- Page entries include filename, side (front/back/single), size_bytes, dimensions (width_px, height_px)
- Dimensions read from actual TIFF headers (use Pillow or equivalent)
- manifest.json written atomically (write to temp file, rename) to avoid partial reads
- pytest/go test passes

title: Scanner session lifecycle manager
description:
Implement the session lifecycle state machine that groups scanned pages into sessions with correct open/close semantics for ADF and flatbed modes.

## Deliverables
- images/document-scanner/scanner-session-manager/session.py
- tests/scanner/test_session.py

## TDD approach
- Red: test ADF session: pages accumulate, session closes when feeder empties
- Red: test flatbed session: pages accumulate, session closes after 90s idle timeout
- Red: test manual close: user triggers close, session ends immediately
- Red: test manual new-document: current session closes, new one opens
- Green: implement SessionManager state machine

## Exit criteria
- ADF mode: session opens on first page, closes when scan returns "no more pages"
- Flatbed mode: session opens on first page, closes after configurable idle timeout (default 90s)
- Manual close supported (for web UI "close session" button)
- Manual new-document supported (close current + open new)
- Session IDs follow YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-hexrand format
- Pages stored as page_001.tiff, page_002.tiff, etc in session directory
- Session directory created under configurable output path
- State machine prevents invalid transitions (e.g. close already-closed session)
- pytest passes with mocked time for idle timeout tests

title: Scanner SANE interface wrapper
description:
Create a Python wrapper around SANE/scanimage CLI for initiating scans and reading scanner status.

## Deliverables
- images/document-scanner/scanner-session-manager/scan.py
- tests/scanner/test_scan.py

## TDD approach
- Red: write tests with a mock/fake scanimage subprocess that returns known output
- Green: implement SaneScanner class that shells out to scanimage with correct params
- Test: correct scanimage CLI args for 600 DPI, color, TIFF, ADF source, flatbed source, duplex

## Exit criteria
- SaneScanner.scan_page() calls scanimage with: --resolution 600, --mode Color, --format tiff, correct --source
- SaneScanner.detect_device() confirms the Epson DS-1630 is available
- SaneScanner.get_status() returns idle/scanning/error
- Output is written to a specified file path
- All scanimage invocations are tested via subprocess mock (no real hardware needed)
- Error handling: device not found, scan failed, USB disconnected mid-scan
- pytest passes
notes: Language: Go (not Python). Go gives a static binary, smaller container image, and better subprocess testing via os/exec mocking.

title: Optical ripper DaemonSet manifest
description:
Create the DaemonSet manifest for the optical disc ripper workload.

## Deliverables
- manifests/optical-ripper/daemonset.yaml
- manifests/optical-ripper/service.yaml (web UI access)

## TDD approach
- Write test that validates DaemonSet manifest structure
- Red: no manifest
- Green: create manifest with correct nodeSelector, resource limits, volume mounts, env vars

## Exit criteria

title: VHS/S-VHS deck-controlled capture workload
description:
Future workload: capture analog video from a professional S-VHS deck with RS-422 machine control.

## Hardware (identified)
- JVC BR-S800U S-VHS playback deck (~$600 shipped from Japan)
- Blackmagic Intensity Shuttle USB 3.0 or similar S-Video ADC (~$200 used)
- USB-to-RS-422 adapter, FTDI-based (~$30) for Sony 9-pin deck control
- Total estimated cost: ~$830

## Key architectural difference: multi-device dependency
This workload requires MULTIPLE USB devices on the same node simultaneously:
1. Video capture card (S-Video + RCA audio input)
2. RS-422 serial adapter (deck transport control)

NFD rules need an AND condition: both devices must be detected on the same node
before the DaemonSet schedules. Options:
- Single NFD rule with multiple matchFeatures (preferred)
- Two labels, nodeSelector requires both
- Custom controller that watches for both labels before creating the workload

This is a new pattern for the framework -- all existing workloads need exactly one USB device.

## Capture workflow
1. Both USB devices detected on node, workload pod scheduled
2. Pod initializes RS-422 connection to deck (Sony 9-pin protocol)
3. User inserts tape, presses play on deck (or triggers via web UI)
4. Pod detects playback start via RS-422 status polling
5. Pod starts recording from V4L2 capture device to FFV1/MKV (lossless)
6. Pod monitors RS-422 for stop/end-of-tape
7. On stop: close file, write metadata, fire notification
8. Web UI shows deck status (play/stop/FF/RW), tape counter, recording status

## Capture parameters
- Video: S-Video input, capture at native resolution (480i NTSC or 576i PAL)
- Audio: RCA stereo, 48kHz 24-bit PCM
- Container: MKV with FFV1 video + PCM audio (lossless archival)
- Estimated file size: ~40-60 GB per hour of content

## Downstream pipeline
- Deinterlace (yadif or QTGMC)
- Noise reduction / stabilization
- Content identification (if commercial release)
- Chapter detection (scene changes, commercial breaks)
- Transcode to H.265 for streaming while keeping FFV1 archival copy

## Open questions
- TBC (timebase correction): does the Blackmagic handle it, or do we need a standalone TBC?
- The BR-S800U is playback-only -- confirm it still responds to RS-422 transport commands
- NTSC vs PAL: the JVC unit from Japan may be NTSC-J only
- Whether to implement full Sony 9-pin protocol or just play/stop/status
- Storage: 60 GB/hour means a 6-hour tape session fills 360 GB

## Status
Idea stage. Hardware identified but not purchased. Interesting because it introduces
the multi-device-dependency pattern which no existing workload uses.

title: SDR / Flipper Zero RF capture workload
description:
Future workload: capture RF signals via USB SDR dongle or Flipper Zero.

## Concept
Same USB hotplug pattern: NFD detects SDR device (RTL-SDR, Flipper Zero in USB mode), DaemonSet schedules capture pod, records IQ samples or demodulated audio to NAS, fires notification on capture completion.

## Hardware
- Flipper Zero with Sub-GHz capabilities (below 1 GHz)
- RTL-SDR dongle (if acquired later, covers up to ~1.7 GHz)
- Flipper Zero presents as USB serial device, RTL-SDR as USB bulk device

## Capture modes (configured, not auto-detected)
- Timed capture: record N minutes of a specific frequency/band
- Signal-triggered: start recording when signal exceeds threshold, stop on silence
- Scheduled pass: for satellite passes (NOAA, ISS SSTV), start/stop at predicted times

## Downstream pipeline depends on signal type
- FM broadcast: demodulate, output as FLAC audio, metadata from RDS
- NOAA weather satellite: decode APT signal to weather imagery
- ADS-B (1090 MHz, needs RTL-SDR): decode aircraft positions, log to database
- Amateur radio: record and archive, transcribe if voice
- Sub-GHz signals (Flipper range): capture and catalog for analysis

## Open questions
- Flipper Zero USB interface: serial vs raw SDR mode, what software drives it
- Whether rtl_sdr / GNU Radio have container-friendly operation
- Session semantics: timed window vs signal detection vs satellite pass scheduler
- Legal considerations for recording certain frequencies (generally fine for receive-only)
- Storage: IQ samples are large (several MB/s), may want to demodulate at capture time

## Status
Idea stage. Flipper Zero hardware is available. Interesting because it extends the framework to non-media ingest.

title: Film/slide scanner capture workload
description:
Future workload: capture photographic film negatives and slides via a dedicated USB film scanner.

## Concept
Same USB hotplug pattern: NFD detects film scanner (e.g. Plustek OpticFilm 8200i, Pacific Image PrimeFilm), DaemonSet schedules capture pod, scans frames to TIFF on NAS, fires notification on roll completion.

## Key differences from document scanning
- Output is photographic (negatives need color inversion, slides do not)
- Dust/scratch removal (Digital ICE hardware or software equivalent)
- Session = one roll of film (24 or 36 frames typically)
- Higher DPI needed (3600-7200 DPI for 35mm to get usable resolution)
- SANE interface shared with document scanner, but scan params and session semantics differ

## Downstream pipeline
- Negative inversion (color profile depends on film stock -- Kodak Gold vs Fuji Superia etc.)
- Dust/scratch removal (if no hardware ICE)
- Date estimation from film stock, frame numbering, or EXIF if the scanner embeds it
- Photo organization: album grouping, location tagging if correlated with other data
- Output: archival TIFF + web-quality JPEG proxy

## Open questions
- Which film scanner? No hardware identified yet.
- SANE support quality for dedicated film scanners varies widely
- Film stock identification (manual tag vs automated)
- Handling of different film formats (35mm, 120/medium format, 4x5 large format)

## Status
Idea only. Backlog until hardware is identified.

title: Vinyl turntable capture workload
description:
Future workload: capture audio from a USB turntable or Bluetooth-connected record player.

## Concept
Same USB hotplug pattern as disc ripper and scanner: NFD detects USB audio device, DaemonSet schedules capture pod, records audio stream to FLAC on NAS, fires notification on session close.

## Key differences from existing workloads
- Session boundary is audio-level based (silence detection), not physical (disc eject, ADF empty)
- Recording is real-time (1:1 with playback duration)
- Input is ALSA/PulseAudio audio capture, not block device or SANE
- Side-flip gap handling needed (do not close session on brief silence between sides)

## Downstream pipeline (Phase 2+)
- Audio fingerprinting (AcoustID/Chromaprint) to identify the album via MusicBrainz
- Track splitting using MusicBrainz durations + silence/gap analysis
- Metadata and album art from MusicBrainz / Cover Art Archive
- Archival format: FLAC (lossless)
- Streaming proxy: Opus or AAC transcode for mobile listening (Navidrome/Jellyfin)

## Open questions
- What USB turntable hardware? No device identified yet.
- Bluetooth vs USB connection (Bluetooth adds latency and compression concerns)
- Audio level threshold for session start/end detection
- How to handle side flips without splitting the session prematurely

## Status
Idea only. No hardware available. Backlog until a turntable is identified and the Phase 2 downstream pipelines (LLM classification, audio fingerprinting) are online.

value: Recognizer optical-ripper end-to-end acceptance test (per user, 2026-05-19): blu-ray loaded in USB drive attached to johnny. Expected flow: (1) ripper detects disc, looks it up via OMDb, copies to the chart's data PVC; (2) on rip-complete, ejects; (3) notifications fire on: rip-start, rip-finish, eject, device-plug-in, device-unplug; (4) already-ripped disc is skipped and ejected with an 'already copied' reason in the eject notification. ARM (Automatic Ripping Machine) provides the rip-skip dedupe via its database. The post-rip hook in images/optical-ripper/hooks/ should already implement the notification side; verify before testing. Device plug/unplug notifications likely need smarter-device-manager or NFD events as the trigger and may need additional implementation if not present.
